inscope.name: One time migration
inscope.description: The One-Time Migration performs the initial transfer of all existing Outlook data to Gmail, including emails, folders, threads, and metadata.

inscope.name: Delta migration
inscope.description: Delta Migration transfers only newly added or modified data after the One-Time Migration.

inscope.name: Inbox
inscope.description:
The Inbox contains all received emails from internal and external users.
Read / Unread: Email read and unread status is preserved
Files: Attachments are migrated with the email
Text Formatting: Bold, italic, underline, bullet list, ordered list, and inline formatting are preserved
Headers: To, From, CC, BCC, Subject fields are retained
External Emails: Sending and receiving emails to/from external users is supported
Mentions: User mentions are retained where supported
Flag / Mark as Unread: Message flags and unread indicators are preserved

inscope.name: Sent
inscope.description: The Sent Items folder stores all emails successfully sent by the user. Sent emails are migrated with recipients, timestamps, and content intact.

inscope.name: Drafts
inscope.description: Emails composed but not sent are migrated and stored in the Drafts folder for further editing.

inscope.name: Junk
inscope.description: Unwanted or spam emails are migrated into the Spam folder in Gmail.

inscope.name: Deleted items
inscope.description: Emails deleted by users are migrated into the Trash folder in Gmail.

inscope.name: Flagged
inscope.description: Emails marked as Flagged in Outlook are migrated as Important or Starred in Gmail.

inscope.name: Custom Folders (Labels)
inscope.description:
User-created folders are migrated as Gmail labels with hierarchy preserved.
 Root Folder: Top-level folders are migrated
Child / Nested Folder: Subfolders maintain their structure
Rules: Outlook rules are applied and emails are placed into corresponding labels

inscope.name: Threads
inscope.description: Email conversations are migrated and maintained as threaded conversations in Gmail.

inscope.name: Timestamp
inscope.description: Original sent and received timestamps are preserved for all migrated emails.

inscope.name: Archive
inscope.description:
Email conversations are migrated and maintained as threaded conversations in Gmail.
The mails which are archived in outlook will migrate to as Archive [Gmail] while migration tool itself create this folder at destination in Gmail.

inscope.name: Distribution Lists / Groups
inscope.description: Emails sent to Outlook distribution lists are migrated and delivered to corresponding Gmail groups, but members are not migrated at destination

inscope.name: Calendars
inscope.description:
Recurring Events: Location, attachments, guests, and recurrence patterns are preserved
 Non-Recurring Events: Single-instance events are migrated
 Past / Present / Future Events: All event timelines are supported

inscope.name: Contacts
inscope.description:
Contact Details: Name, phone numbers, email addresses, and notes are migrated
Contact Photos: Photos are not migrated; all other details are preserved

inscope.name: Shared Mailbox
inscope.description: Shared mailboxes accessible by multiple users are migrated while preserving shared access.

inscope.name: Shared Calendars
inscope.description: Shared calendars are migrated with permissions, allowing users to add events and manage access.

inscope.name: Group Calendars
inscope.description: Group calendars are migrated with sharing permissions, allowing users to add events and manage access.

inscope.name: Read / Unread Functionality
inscope.description: Read and Unread status of emails is fully preserved during migration. Emails marked as read in Outlook will appear as read in Gmail, and unread emails remain unread. This status is also maintained during Delta Migration.

inscope.name: signature
inscope.description: we support signature for Outlook to Gmail

inscope.name: primary calendar
inscope.description: primary calendar is the default calendar tied to your mailbox/account. When someone sends you a meeting, it lands in your primary calendar. Your availability (free/busy) is taken from the primary calendar. we can create events in the primary calendar.

inscope.name: Secondary calendar
inscope.description: A secondary calendar is A calendar you create manually or add from another source, separate from your main (primary) calendar and used for organization, categorization, or sharing. we can create events in the secondary calendar as well.

inscope.name: Recipient Writing
inscope.description: Recipients are the people who receive an email (To, Cc, and Bcc). During migration, recipient details are preserved because they are part of the email data. After migration, the recipient addresses are mapped and associated with the destination domain usernames, ensuring proper identification and communication in the new environment.

inscope.name: single instance calendar
inscope.description:
single instance calendar in both primary and secondary calendar it is migrated perfectly and the status response is also stored 
after migration we have equivalent attendees with destination domain user, Teams links are converted to Google Meet links, attendee response states are preserved 
, attachments, location and attendees are migrated successfully.

inscope.name: Calendar — Permissions / Delegates
inscope.description: Calendar permissions and delegates allow users to access and manage another user’s calendar. During migration, delegate permissions are mapped to Google Calendar’s “Make changes and manage sharing,” though some advanced features may not fully transfer, and we can access private event also which is created by organizer

inscope.name: Attachments associated with past calendar invites
inscope.description: we support attachments associated with past calendar invites
inscope.family: Attachments associated with past calendar invites

inscope.name: Busy Status in Calendar event
inscope.description: we migrated busy status from outlook to Gmail and if we are selecting other status like free, out of office, tentative, working elsewhere these are migrated as with status busy only, and we don't migrate deleted events

inscope.name: Contacts with any one empty field
inscope.description: In contacts by giving one field and remaining fields as empty we are migrating
inscope.family: Contacts with any one empty field

inscope.name: High-importance emails
inscope.description: high-importance emails from Outlook are seamlessly migrated to Gmail and are appropriately labeled under the ‘Important’ category to maintain their priority.

outscope.name: Categories not Preserved
outscope.description: Emails are migrated, but category information is completely lost, and no corresponding labels are created in Gmail.

outscope.name: Sensitivity Labels / Information Protection Labels
outscope.description:
The Sensitivity / classification value shown in Outlook is not returned by Microsoft Graph API for this message.
Outlook may display this tag based on internal Exchange or Purview metadata that is not exposed through the API.

Because the value is not available in the API response, it cannot be retrieved or migrated.
This is a Microsoft Graph API limitation.

outscope.name: emoji folder name not preserved
outscope.description: Gmail API has a length limitation for label names (approximately 225 characters). The source label contains a large number of Unicode emoji characters, which exceeds the maximum size allowed by Gmail. When this limit is exceeded, the Gmail API may return a backend error instead of creating the label. Because of this API limitation, very long label names cannot be created in Gmail and must be shortened during migration.

outscope.name: Conversation History folder not preserved
outscope.description: This folder contains chat history and communication logs from applications such as Skype, Teams, or Lync, and does not store regular email messages. Since the migration process only supports standard email folders, the Conversation History folder is excluded from migration.

outscope.name: Notes migration is not preserved
outscope.description: Notes are not migrated when Outlook is used as the source. This is because Notes in Outlook do not contain emails. They are personal notes created by the user and are not part of the mailbox data. The migration process only supports email and mailbox-related items, so Notes are not included in the migration.

outscope.name: contact categories
outscope.description: Contact categories in Outlook are not retrievable through Microsoft's API — the category tag information assigned to contacts is not exposed as part of the contact data returned by the API.

outscope.name: contact lists/groups
outscope.description: Google Contacts does not support contact group structures, meaning there is no feature or equivalent in Google Contacts that can hold or represent a collection of contacts as a group. This is a Google-side limitation that prevents contact groups from being migrated to the destination.

outscope.name: pinned mails
outscope.description: Pinned emails will be migrated, but they will not remain pinned in the destination ​

outscope.name: Notes
outscope.description: Outlook Notes are not migrated because Gmail does not have an equivalent feature to store them, and migration tools do not support transferring note items

outscope.name: Encrypted and non-encrypted
outscope.description: Encrypted and non‑encrypted mail tags indicate the security status of emails in Outlook. Although the emails are migrated, these tags are not preserved because they are part of Microsoft’s encryption system, which is platform-specific and has no equivalent in Gmail.

outscope.name: To Do list
outscope.description: Outlook To‑Do list (tasks) is not migrated because Gmail does not have an equivalent task structure and migration tools do not support transferring task items.

outscope.name: Any invites created by external users
outscope.description: When migrating calendar events where an external user is the organizer or creator, the system automatically triggers a notification to that external user because calendar protocols (such as iCalendar/RFC 5545) treat any change to an event's data — including moving it to a new system — as a modification to the original event. Since the external user is the legitimate owner of that event, the calendar system is designed to alert them whenever their event is altered by another party, even if the change is purely administrative like a migration. This is a built-in protection mechanism of calendar platforms (Google Calendar, Outlook, etc.) to ensure event owners are always informed of any changes made to events they organize or created, and it cannot be bypassed without either excluding such events from the migration scope or suppressing outbound notifications at the system level during the migration window.
outscope.family: Any invites created by external users

outscope.name: Attendees will not receive calendar events for past events after migration
outscope.description: When migrating past non-recurring calendar events, attendees will not receive the migrated event on their calendars because these events are intentionally migrated only for the creator/organizer, not for the attendees. Since the event has already occurred and will not repeat in the future, sending calendar invites to attendees' post-migration would serve no practical purpose and would instead cause confusion by delivering notifications or calendar entries for events that have already passed. To avoid unnecessary disruption and inbox clutter for attendees, the migration tool is designed to restore past, non-recurring events solely to the creator's calendar as a historical record, while attendees' calendars are left unchanged.
outscope.family: Attendees will not receive calendar events for past events after migration

outscope.name: Legal Hold data
outscope.description: Legal Hold emails cannot be migrated with their complete metadata because the API does not provide access to metadata for emails that are under Legal Hold. Legal Hold is a compliance and legal preservation mechanism that restricts and locks down data to prevent any alteration, access, or extraction beyond what is legally permitted, and as a result, the email platform's API deliberately blocks metadata retrieval for such emails to maintain the integrity of the legal preservation process. Since the migration tool relies entirely on API access to fetch and transfer email data including its metadata (such as timestamps, sender/receiver details, and headers), it is technically unable to retrieve or migrate this information for Legal Hold emails, and this is a platform-level restriction that is outside the scope of the migration tool's control.

outscope.name: Admin or user settings
outscope.description: Admin and user settings will not be migrated to the destination system because Microsoft's API does not provide access to or expose these configurations in a way that can be extracted and transferred. Settings such as mailbox preferences, rules, permissions, and other administrative or user-level configurations are managed internally by Microsoft and are not available through their API for migration purposes.

outscope.name: Calendar owner scope
outscope.description: For a calendar event to be migrated successfully, the calendar owner must be included in the scope of the migration. Events belonging to users outside the migration scope will not be transferred.

outscope.name: Calendar attachment size varies
outscope.description: Attachment sizes in Google are determined by Google's own storage and encoding mechanisms. In some cases, the attachment size in the destination may be larger than in the source or vice versa, resulting in a size difference between the two environments. This is expected behavior and not an indication of data loss or corruption.

outscope.name: Mailbox policy
outscope.description: If a policy is applied to a mailbox, emails and their attachments will not be migrated or shared. Ensure that any such policies are reviewed and handled before initiating the migration to avoid data being skipped.

outscope.name: Group Members
outscope.description: In distribution list groups will be migrated but members are not created at destination

outscope.name: In place Achieve
outscope.description: In-Place Archive in Outlook is a secondary mailbox feature in Microsoft 365 (Exchange) that gives users extra storage for older or less frequently accessed emails — without leaving Outlook.

outscope.name: Rooms/ Resources
outscope.description: A Room in Outlook Calendar is a resource mailbox that allows users to book and manage meeting rooms automatically, preventing scheduling conflicts.

outscope.name: Calendar — Recurring Series​
outscope.description:
In recurring meeting where we have modified one occurrence and deleted another, then performed migration. After migration, the modified occurrence did not show the changes and the deleted occurrence reappeared in Google Calendar.
As per the developer, this happens because Outlook stores such changes and deletions as exceptions within the recurring series, but Google Calendar does not support an equivalent structure. Due to this platform mismatch, modified and deleted occurrences cannot be mapped correctly during migration.

outscope.name: Email rules and forwarding rules
outscope.description: We don’t support migration of email rules and forwarding settings from Outlook to Gmail. This is because Microsoft APIs do not expose rule and forwarding configurations, so the migration tool cannot access this data. Additionally, Outlook and Gmail use completely different rule engines with no direct mapping between them. Hence, due to both API limitations and platform incompatibility, these settings cannot be migrated and must be recreated manually in Gmail.

outscope.name: Contact pictures
outscope.description: we don't support contact pictures

outscope.name: Attachment with link is migrated as source link
outscope.description: Attachment with link which is migrated from source is opened in the Microsoft only it won't open in the Gmail because we are just copying attachment from the source it does not open in the google drive
outscope.family: Attachment with is migrated as source link

A custom label in Gmail is a way to group similar emails into categories, so they are easy to find and manage later.

Nested label (Sub-label): A label created inside a root label, used to divide main categories further.
Child label (Sub-sub label): A label inside a nested label, more specific level of organization.

inscope.name: Filters/rules

If those emails appear under the correct folder or label after migration, they are considered successfully migrated. The filter only controls organization and does not affect the migration status of the emails.

inscope.description: The One-Time Migration performs the initial transfer of all existing Gmail data to another Gmail account, including emails, labels, threads, and metadata.

inscope.name: Delta migration
inscope.description: Delta Migration transfers only newly added or modified data after the One-Time Migration between Gmail accounts.

inscope.name: Inbox
inscope.description:
Read / Unread: Email read and unread status is preserved.
        Files: Attachments are migrated with the email.
       Text Formatting: Bold, italic, underline, bullet list, ordered list, and inline formatting are preserved.
       Headers: To, From, CC, BCC, Subject fields are retained.
       External Emails: Sending and receiving emails to/from external users is supported.
       Mentions: User mentions are retained where supported.
       Flag / Star / Mark as Unread: Message indicators are preserved.

inscope.name: Sent
inscope.description: Sent emails are migrated with recipients, timestamps, and content intact.

inscope.name: Drafts
inscope.description: Draft emails are migrated and stored for further editing.

inscope.name: Junk / Spam
inscope.description: Unwanted or spam emails are migrated to the Junk/Spam folder.

inscope.name: Deleted / Trash
inscope.description: Deleted emails are migrated to the Deleted/Trash folder.

inscope.name: Starred
inscope.description: Starred mails are migrated to starred folders .

inscope.name: Custom Folders (Labels)
inscope.description:
Root Folder: Top-level custom folders are migrated.
       Child / Nested Folder: Subfolders maintain their parent-child structure.
       Rules / Filters: Existing rules or filters are applied where supported.

inscope.name: Threads
inscope.description: Email conversations with multiple replies are migrated as threaded conversations to maintain continuity.

inscope.name: Timestamp
inscope.description: Original sent and received timestamps are preserved for all migrated emails.

inscope.name: All Mail (Gmail Only)
inscope.description: The Gmail-specific “All Mail” view is migrated while preserving email visibility across folders.

inscope.name: Calendars
inscope.description:
Recurring Events: Location, attachments, guests, and recurrence patterns are preserved.
        Non-Recurring Events: Single-instance events are migrated.
        Past / Present / Future Events: All event timelines are supported.

inscope.name: Contacts
inscope.description:
Contact Details: Name, phone numbers, email addresses, and notes are migrated.
       Contact Photos: Photos are migrated if supported.

inscope.name: Shared Mailbox
inscope.description: Shared or delegated mailboxes are migrated while preserving access permissions where supported.

inscope.name: Group Mail Migration
inscope.description: Emails sent to groups are migrated and delivered to all group members in the destination environment.

inscope.name: Group Calendars
inscope.description: Group calendars are migrated with sharing permissions, allowing users to add events and manage access.
